en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tikaṇikārapupphiya Kaṇikāra Chapter 1 The Apadāna of the Elder Tikaṇikārapupphiya: I was a monk in the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa, And I offered three kaṇikāra flowers to the Teacher. Because of that kamma, I have been reborn in heaven for a hundred thousand aeons; Now, having passed away from there, I have been born here in the human world. I am now a monk in the dispensation of the Buddha Gotama, Possessing the six supernormal powers and the triple knowledge. Having attained the peaceful state, I dwell in the bliss of Nibbāna. This is the fruit of offering flowers to the Buddha. Thus, one should offer fragrant flowers to the Buddha, For this is the path to the attainment of Nibbāna. By honoring the Buddha with flowers, one attains heavenly realms; Having honored him with flowers, one reaches the state beyond death. “The Fully Enlightened One named Sumedha,
endowed with the thirty-two excellent marks,
the Fully Enlightened One who desires solitude— ”
I approached the Himavat mountains.
Having plunged into the Himalayas,
the foremost, compassionate Sage—
Having folded his legs crosswise,
the Supreme Person sat down;
at that time, I was a master of the sciences (vidyādhara).
I was a wanderer through the sky;
taking up a well-fashioned trident,
I then traveled through the atmosphere.
Like a fire on a mountain peak,
like the moon on the full-moon day,
the Buddha shines in the forest.
Like a king of sal trees in full bloom,
having emerged from the forest edge,
the rays of the Buddha rushed forth.
Seeing those [flowers] resembling the color of a flame, my mind became serene.
As I searched, I saw a flower.
Taking three *kaṇikāra* flowers, which possess the fragrance of the gods,
I made an offering to the Best of Buddhas.
Through the power of the Buddha,
those three flowers of mine at that time had their stalks turned upward and their petals downward.
They provide shade for the Teacher.
By that well-performed deed,
and by their volition and aspiration, [they attain this].
Having abandoned my human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three.
There, a well-constructed celestial mansion was mine.
It is known as Kaṇikārī;
it is sixty yojanas high and thirty yojanas wide.
With a thousand shafts and a hundred joints,
made of green bamboo and adorned with banners,
it had a hundred thousand projections.
There appeared before me mansions made of gold, made of gems,
and also made of ruby.
Crystal couches as well,
arranged as one desires and in whatever way one wishes,
and costly beds.
Furnished with cotton mattresses,
entirely covered with wool,
and provided with pillows.
Having emerged from meditation,
while wandering on my journey through the realms of the gods,
whenever I desire to go—
Honored by the assembly of gods,
I stand beneath the flower,
with it as my canopy above.
For a hundred leagues all around,
it was covered with *kaṇikāra* flowers.
Sixty thousand musical instruments—
Attending upon me morning and evening,
they constantly wait on me day and night without weariness.
There, with dances, songs,
cymbals, and instrumental music,
I delighted in the pleasure of play.
I rejoice here, desiring my desires.
Having eaten and drunk there,
I then rejoice among the Thirty-three gods.
Accompanied by hosts of women,
I rejoice in this supreme celestial mansion;
five hundred times over.
I exercised the sovereignty of the gods;
and three hundred times,
I was a wheel-turning monarch.
A vast regional sovereignty,
beyond counting and incalculable;
wandering through various states of existence, I attained it.
I obtain great enjoyment;
there is no deficiency in my enjoyments—
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
I wander through two states of existence,
as a deva and as a human;
I know no other destination.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha:
I am born into two families,
among both kshatriyas and brahmins.
I am not born into a lowly family;
this is the fruit of my worship of the Buddha.
[I possess] elephant-vehicles and horse-vehicles.
A palanquin and a carriage;
I obtain all of this—
it is the fruit of this worship of the Buddha.
A multitude of female slaves, a multitude of male slaves,
and women beautifully adorned—
I obtain all of this.
This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha:
silken garments, woolen blankets,
and those made of linen and cotton.
I obtain all of this;
it is the fruit of this worship of the Buddha.
A new cloth, a new fruit—
I obtain all these nine kinds of flavorful foods;
this is the fruit of my worship of the Buddha.
"Eat this, enjoy this,
lie down on this bed;
I obtain all of this."
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha:
everywhere I am honored,
and my fame has spread far and wide.
I am always one with a great following,
always having an unbreakable assembly;
I am the foremost among my kinsmen.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha:
I know neither cold nor heat,
and no feverish distress exists.
Furthermore, mental suffering does not exist within my heart;
having become golden-hued, I am radiant.
I transmigrate through various states of existence;
I did not know of this disfigurement—
this is the fruit of my worship of the Buddha.
Having passed away from the world of the gods,
impelled by the root of his wholesome merit,
he was born in the city of Sāvatthī.
In Mahāsāla, which was very wealthy,
I abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure and went forth into the homeless life.
At the age of seven,
I attained arahantship;
the Buddha ordained me.
Recognizing my virtue, the Visionary One said:
"Though young, I am worthy of honor;
this is the fruit of my worship of the Buddha."
My divine eye is purified;
I am skilled in concentration;
I have reached perfection in direct knowledge.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha:
having attained the analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā),
he is skilled in the bases of psychic power (iddhipāda).
Having reached perfection in all phenomena—
this is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
Thirty thousand eons ago,
Because I worshipped the Buddha,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
The defilements have been incinerated by me;
all states of existence have been uprooted;
like a nāga who has severed its bonds, I am free.
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me in the presence of the Buddha.
The three true insights have been attained;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges—
And these eight liberations have been attained;
the six direct knowledges have been realized—
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.”
Thus indeed the venerable elder Tikaṇikārapupphiya spoke these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Tikaṇikārapupphiya.
